title: Big bands that came to Louisville, and trying to recall one
summary: Her father drove her and her friends to dances when the big bands came to town. She recalls Earl Hines and Duke Ellington, met Lunceford only later in Buffalo, knew Fletcher and Horace Henderson, and cannot place the band Dance is asking about.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: That's the truth. That happens so many time. My father used to take us to the dances when the big bands would come to town. And Papa would take me and my little friends that live out where I lived. Take us to the dance and then he'd come and pick us up when the dance was over. And now I hear all these big bands and things and I'm older than all.
They knew what to do?
Yeah, and they did it.
Who do you remember? What bands do you remember particularly in those days?
Oh, Earl "Father" Hines, Duke Ellington. But, what is his name . . .
Lunceford?
Well, Jimmie Lunceford, I met him

when I first came to Buffalo, New York. I didn't know him before then.
Bennie Moten?
No, I didn't know about Bennie Moten. But . . .
Was it the Territory Band?
No.
It was a big band?
Yes.
Not Calloway?
Not Calloway.
Fletcher Henderson?
Fletcher Henderson I knew. And then his brother Horace Henderson, because mostly boys used to play with him, Horace. But this . . .
You don't mean Fats Waller or anybody like that?
No.
It doesn't matter. If they come to you, we'll think about it.
It was right on the tip of my tongue.
Not Bobby Johnson?
